messages:
Maria: FYI linux/bazel smoke CI is red after yesterday's toolchain image roll. Failing compile in //runtime:fastpath with error:

```
/usr/include/c++/10/atomic: In function '...':
error: undefined reference to '__atomic_load_8'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```

This looks like an ABI/libstdc++ change, started at ~03:20 UTC in the job logs.

Jon: Hmm, saw something similar on the mac image roll last week. Can you paste the failing target and the exact bazel command used by CI?

Maria: Failing target is //runtime/fastpath:fastpath_bin. CI runs:
```
bazel build --config=linux_x86_64 --compiler=gcc-11 //runtime/fastpath:fastpath_bin
```

Arjun: We promoted a gcc-12 base image to the linux pool last night (toolchain roll). Suspect the newer libstdc++/atomic behavior. Quick tries: either force the old image in CI or add explicit -latomic to the target linkopts.

Sophie: I'm starting a rerun on that shard now :eyes: https://ci.company/1234 (rerun triggered). If it passes intermittently we should bisect. @ci-bot any metadata about the roll?

ci-bot: Toolchain image roll id=toolchain-roll-20260316 promoted gcc-12.1.0 -> linux-x86_64 pool at 2026-03-16T03:42:07Z. No other infra changes in the window.

Jon: Ok that matches. Maria, can you try to reproduce locally inside a gcc-12 container (bazel clean --expunge before build)? That should confirm it's the toolchain.

Maria: Reproduced locally with gcc:12 container. Same undefined reference. Quick local fix: linking with -latomic fixes the link error for the third_party/fastmath object.

Arjun: That implies libatomic isn't automatically linked with the newer libstdc++ in our build config. I'll draft a tiny PR adding linkopts = ["-latomic"] to //runtime/fastpath:fastpath_lib and run canary.

Sophie: If small, we can merge and do a canary rollout to Dedicated and re-run smoke to validate. Also add a note in the toolchain-roll checklist to test symbols used by third_party native libs.

Maria: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inc/runtime/pull/482 — includes linkopts and a CI-only sanity target. Kicking CI.

Jon: Nice. If CI passes on canary, we should backfill a follow-up to audit other native deps.

Arjun: Agreed. Will also add a short blurb in the infra roll notes.

Sophie: Thanks all. Keeping this thread for final status. If rerun flakes again, we'll run bisection on toolchain images across gcc-11 -> gcc-12.
